sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Setup and imports (part 1)
sections.what: Loads the tools and paths the checks need, including the list of model-backed interfaces. It sets up the comparison between the hand-written TypeScript shapes and the Python models.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Setup and imports (part 2)
sections.what: Finishes the setup for the checks in this file. It names the frontend types file that the mirror checks read.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: declared_fields
sections.title: Reading declared field names
sections.what: Reads the field names that each hand-written interface declares in the frontend types file. The two comparison tests use these names.
sections.why: Likely reason: the checks need one shared way to read field names, so both tests compare the same kind of list.
sections.watch_out: The reader depends on the exact text layout of the interface declarations, so a formatting change could make it read nothing.

sections.name: TestTheParserWorks
sections.title: Confirming the parser reads real interfaces
sections.what: Tests the field name reader on known inputs so that a broken reader cannot make the comparison tests pass.
sections.why: Likely reason: an empty reader would make every comparison pass, so it needs its own check.

sections.name: TestTheExemptionsAreLive
sections.title: Confirming the exemptions are in use
sections.what: Checks that each listed exemption still matches a real model field and a real interface. This stops stale exemptions from hiding gaps.
sections.why: Likely reason: an exemption that outlives its reason would silently hide a future drift.

sections.name: TestEveryMirrorMatchesItsModel
sections.title: Each mirror must match its model
sections.what: For every interface with a Python model, fails if the frontend is missing a field the model has, or declares a field the model does not have. Exempted fields are skipped.
sections.why: The viewer cannot show a field it does not know about, and a field read but never written shows as undefined with no error.
sections.watch_out: Each mirror must also be listed in the model map, or this test never checks it.

summary: Checks that hand-written TypeScript interfaces in the artifacts file list the same field names as the Python models they copy, allowing only a short, documented list of deliberate differences.
purpose: Catch field names that drift apart between the viewer's hand-written types and the engine's Python models.
why: The artifacts file is not generated, so this is its only guard. The header says that field names are compared rather than types, because the spelling of types differs for legitimate reasons.
how: Pairs each TypeScript interface with its Python model. Reads field names from the TypeScript text and compares them with the model's fields, skipping documented exceptions. Also checks that each exception is still needed.
inputs: The artifacts TypeScript file, plus the list of Python model classes and the list of named exceptions in the file.
outputs: Pytest results. A failure names any field present on one side only, or any exception that is no longer needed.
risks: Field names are read with a text pattern, so unusual formatting could be missed. The exception list is maintained by hand. Only names are compared, so type mismatches are not caught. Only five of the six checks were available for review when these notes were written.
debug: If the parser test fails, the layout of the artifacts file has changed. If a field mismatch appears, compare that field name on both sides. If the exception test fails, remove the exception from the list.
